issues.legal_issue: A possession decree against one tenant is binding in execution on other family members who succeeded to the same undivided tenancy, even if they were not joined in the suit.
material_facts: The original tenant died while a minor son was residing with him; the son claimed tenancy rights as a member of the tenant’s family.
After the original tenant’s death, rent bills were issued in the name of one son and later that son’s widow, whom the landlord accepted as tenant.
The premises and rent were not divided, and the claimant said that rent was paid through the widow rather than separately by him.
The landlord obtained a consent decree against the widow, and the claimant and his family objected to its execution on the ground that they had not been parties to the suit.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy was a single tenancy that devolved jointly on the qualifying family members. The widow represented the tenants in the suit, so the decree was binding on the other members covered by the tenancy and could be executed against them; they could not resist execution merely because they were not joined.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(11)(c) of the Bombay Rent Act, 1947 includes a member of the tenant’s family residing with the tenant at the time of death, subject to agreement among the family members or a court decision in default of agreement. Applying Ganpath Ladha v. Sashikant Vishnu Shinde, the Court noted the protective purpose of rent legislation without extinguishing landlords’ property rights. Under Kanji Manji v. Trustees of the Port of Bombay, a suit against one joint tenant is maintainable and its decree binds the others. H.C. Pandey v. G.C. Paul establishes that, absent a contrary provision, the tenancy devolves as a single tenancy on the heirs, without division of premises or rent. Textile Association (India), Bombay Unit v. Balmohan Gopal Kurup was distinguished on its facts.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and family_member_resided_with_tenant_at_death and tenancy_remained_undivided and decree_obtained_against_accepted_tenant

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party objects to enforcement of a possession decree in an execution proceeding.
predicates.family_member_resided_with_tenant_at_dea: The person claiming tenancy rights was a member of the tenant’s family and resided with the tenant when the tenant died.
predicates.tenancy_remained_undivided: The premises and rent were not divided into separate tenancies among the successors.
predicates.decree_obtained_against_accepted_tenant: The landlord obtained the decree against a successor whom the landlord had accepted as the tenant.

issues.definition: When an execution objection is brought by a qualifying family successor to an undivided tenancy, a decree obtained against an accepted tenant binds the other successors to that tenancy.

issues.legal_issue: A person found not to have occupied the premises for years before the eviction suit need not be joined as a defendant and cannot obstruct execution on the ground of nonjoinder.
material_facts: The trial and appellate courts concurrently found that the claimant had left the premises while his elder brother was alive and had not resided there since then.
The claimant had moved elsewhere, acquired other accommodation, and used an address elsewhere for correspondence at work.
The landlord sued the widow who was named on the rent bills, and the claimant objected to execution because he had not been joined.
issues.conclusion: Because the claimant had not been residing in the premises since long before the eviction suit, the landlord had no cause of action to recover possession from him and was not required to join him. The claimant therefore had no justification to resist execution.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the concurrent factual findings that the claimant was not residing in the premises when the eviction suit was filed. In those circumstances, there was no cause of action for the landlord to seek possession from him, and his nonjoinder did not make the decree invalid or inexecutable.

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party objects to enforcement of a possession decree in an execution proceeding.
predicates.claimant_not_residing_when_suit_filed: The claimant had ceased residing in the premises well before the landlord filed the eviction suit.
predicates.possession_claim_not_directed_against_cl: The landlord sought possession from the tenant in occupation rather than from the absent claimant.

issues.definition: If a claimant was not residing in the premises when the eviction suit was filed and the possession claim was not directed against that claimant, the claimant cannot resist execution because they were not joined.
